title: Judge a contested question by whether its answer is correct

intentCoverage.report:
Verdict: Caught.

Story and revision: SEED-073#judge-contested-question-by-answer-correctness ("Judge a contested question by whether its answer is correct"), plan .planning/slice-plans/102-judge-contested-question-by-answer-correctness/PLAN.md, revision 4413fd8ee8b24fd1bf586fd79133b15bf664754e (branch claude/judge-a-contested-question-by-whether-its-answer).

Promise: the contest is refused only when the supported choices are exactly the stored answer; it is accepted otherwise, including when more than one choice is defensible (note supports choices 1 and 3, stored choice 1 -> accepted, advice names both, replacement follows).

Fault (caller suggestion, used unchanged after validation): backend/src/main/java/com/odde/donut/services/ai/SupportedChoices.java, contestResult:
  - result.rejected = stored.length == 1 && Arrays.equals(supportedChoices, stored);
  + result.rejected = stored.length == 1 && Arrays.stream(supportedChoices).anyMatch(i -> i == stored[0]);
This refuses a contest whenever the stored answer is among the supported choices, so supported [0, 2] with stored 0 is wrongly refused. No fixture or assertion was changed.

Maintained check: RecallPromptContestControllerTest.Accepted.whenTheNoteSupportsMoreThanOneChoice (stubs the model to return supportedChoices [0, 2] for the "red/black/green" MCQ with stored answer 0, calls controller.contest, asserts rejected is false, advice contains the note supports "red", "green", and the MCQ is marked contested).

Runs (scratch detached worktree at the selected revision, prepared with scripts/worktree_setup.sh; clean git status before the probe; focused command CURSOR_DEV=true nix develop -c ./backend/gradlew -p backend test -Dspring.profiles.active=test --tests 'com.odde.donut.controllers.RecallPromptContestControllerTest'):
- Baseline: 12 tests, 0 failures (outer class 7, Accepted 5). Reach confirmed: the JUnit XML lists whenTheNoteSupportsMoreThanOneChoice() as executed and passing.
- Faulted: 12 tests, 1 failure, the only failure being Accepted.whenTheNoteSupportsMoreThanOneChoice, at its first assertion assertFalse(contest.rejected) (RecallPromptContestControllerTest.java:90): "expected: <false> but was: <true>". That is the wrong behavior seen directly on the intended path: the controller's verdict for supported [0, 2] with stored 0 came back as refused. refusedWhenTheNoteSupportsExactlyTheStoredAnswer and the other Accepted cases still passed, as expected, because the fault matches the correct verdict for those inputs.
- Restored: the file was copied back by an EXIT trap. git status in the scratch worktree was empty before and after the restored run. Rerun: 12 tests, 0 failures. Scratch worktree removed with git worktree remove --force.

Claim limit: the check covers only the controller-level verdict for a two-choice support set that includes the stored answer. The probe did not exercise the advice text or the replacement step under this fault, because the earlier assertion failed first.

Next proof action: none needed for this promise and path. The maintained assertion already catches the fault.
Prior disposition: this matches the story's key example and the rewritten test the plan intended. No new repair decision came from the probe.

Costs:
- Test runtime (measured, Gradle wall clock "BUILD SUCCESSFUL/FAILED in"): baseline 41s, faulted 28s, restored 21s; about 90s in total. JUnit-reported suite time per run was about 13-18s.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part during the probe, and no separate measure exists.
- Agent effort: unavailable. No separately supported token or time measure of agent work is available to this agent.
- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 278985 ms (measured), from 1794920978519 to 1794921257504 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.
